introduction: Forty days after Christmas, Mary and Joseph bring the child Jesus to the Temple to present him to the Lord. There the old man Simeon takes him in his arms and calls him "a light for revelation to the nations," and the prophetess Anna speaks of him to everyone waiting for redemption. Today candles are blessed as a sign of Christ our light, and the Church keeps the World Day for Consecrated Life. Let us welcome the Lord who comes to his temple.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, with Simeon and Anna we welcome Christ, the light of the nations. Let us pray with confidence.
intentions: For the Church: that she may carry the light of Christ to every nation and every heart. Let us pray to the Lord.

For consecrated men and women, on this World Day for Consecrated Life: that, like Anna, they may serve God with prayer night and day, and bring joy to all who look for redemption. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the elderly, especially those who are lonely or forgotten: that, like Simeon and Anna, they may know that their faith and their waiting are precious to God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For parents and families: that they may present their children to the Lord and raise them in wisdom and grace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who walk in darkness: that the light of Christ may give them hope and peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Father, your Son was presented in the Temple and revealed as the light of the nations. Let that light shine in our hearts and in our world. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: A light for the nations
reflection.body:
Malachi promised that "The Lord, whom you seek, will suddenly come to his temple." Israel may have imagined a dramatic entrance. Instead the Lord arrives in his mother's arms, brought by a poor couple who can offer only "A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons," the offering the Law allowed for families of modest means.

Simeon has waited his whole life for this moment. The Holy Spirit had told him he would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ. Now he takes the child in his arms and prays: "Now you are releasing your servant, Master, according to your word, in peace; for my eyes have seen your salvation." The Church makes his words her own every night in Night Prayer.

Simeon also sees further than the joy of the moment. He tells Mary that her son will be "a sign which is spoken against," and that "a sword will pierce through your own soul." The light of Christ will shine fully only through the cross.

Anna, a widow of great age, "didn't depart from the temple, worshiping with fastings and petitions night and day." She is the patron of all who give their lives to prayer, and today the Church thanks God for consecrated men and women whose lives, like hers, are spent in waiting on the Lord and pointing others to him.

The Letter to the Hebrews explains why Jesus shared our flesh and blood: so that he could be "a merciful and faithful high priest," one who "is able to help those who are tempted." Take home a blessed candle if your parish offers one. Light it when you pray this year, and let it remind you that the light Simeon held in his arms now shines in your home.
